summary: Pricing tag rename caused eco-flag tariff on embedding batch — unexpected surcharge on monthly invoice
description:
Issue summary:
Customer noticed a one-off tariff labeled 'eco-flag' applied to multiple embedding batch line items on their March invoice. The customer has a negotiated exemption and expected the negotiated enterprise embed rate. Impact: invoice shows ~+$3,200 in surcharges attributed to 'eco-flag' for embedding jobs between 2026-02-28 and 2026-03-02.

Impact:
- ClearVoice AI flagged unexpected +$3.2k charge on finalized invoice.
- Billing team unable to reconcile with customer's rate agreement.
- Customer is concerned this will repeat next cycle and asked for immediate credit and an explanation.

Environment:
- Production, us-east-1.
- Affected jobs: nightly batch embeddings triggered via /v1/embeddings route (route-id: embed-batch-02).

Steps to reproduce / observed chain:
1) Customer ran scheduled batch on 2026-02-28 23:45 UTC.
2) Postbacks for those jobs arrived to billing pipeline 2026-03-01 00:02 UTC.
3) Billing reconciler applied pricing_tag 'eco-flag' to multiple postbacks and classified them under eco surcharge tier.
4) Console and API showed normal usage; no toolcall or experimental flags set by customer.

Expected behavior:
- Postbacks from enterprise org should resolve to negotiated embed rate; no eco surcharge should be applied.

Actual behavior:
- Postbacks resolved to default eco surcharge tariff due to a pricing_tag value present on postbacks. Customer console did not show this tag.

Logs / Attachments:
- Customer provided invoice PDF and sample postback payloads (attached).
- Billing reconciler logs (samples) attached; reconciler shows pricing_tag="eco-v1" on several postbacks.

Customer request:
- Immediate provisional credit for the $3,200.
- Root cause analysis and steps to prevent recurrence.
- Confirmation that historical usage will be re-rated if this is a Redwood-side mapping problem.
comments: 2026-03-10 15:12 - Maya Chen: Opened ticket after initial call with customer. Customer provided invoice and two example postbacks. Requested provisional credit and RCA.

2026-03-10 16:05 - Billing Team (Ana Ruiz): Investigating whether pricing_tag was inlined by the postback-emitter in the customer's SDK or mapped during our postback normalization. Requesting raw postback receipts and reconciler logs.

2026-03-10 18:20 - SRE (Jon Park): Found recent infra change to pricing-tag aliases deployed 2026-02-27 (PR #2891). That change introduced an alias mapping, adding 'eco-v1' to default alias set when no explicit enterprise_tag present. Digging into reconciler behavior.

2026-03-11 09:45 - Liam O'Connor: Reached out to ClearVoice contact (account manager) to explain we are investigating and will provisionally credit while investigation continues per enterprise SLA. Customer acknowledged and requested ETA for permanent fix.
2026-03-11 12:30 - Billing Engineer (Priya Singh): Confirmed provisional credit created in invoicing system (provision_id: PC-8712). Awaiting postback replay to confirm re-rating path.
2026-03-12 08:10 - Maya Chen: Customer accepted provisional credit and asked for communication to include mitigation so they can avoid manual checks next month.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: customer postback included explicit 'pricing_tag' value 'eco-v1' resulting in eco surcharge.
Checked customer-provided postbacks: none of the payloads set 'enterprise_pricing_id' or 'override_tag'. They include a null enterprise field and a generated pricing_tag by staging proxies.

Reviewed PR github.com/redwood/infra/pull/2891: change introduced aliasing behavior for legacy postbacks where missing enterprise tag would map to a fallback set that included 'eco-v1'. Deployed 2026-02-27 03:15 UTC.

Billing reconciler behavior: when enterprise_pricing_id is missing, use alias mapping to infer tariff. Alias table contained 'eco-v1' as highest-priority alias for certain embed routes due to a tagging rule that was too broad.
Frequency: ~42% of customer's batch postbacks in window were rated with 'eco-v1' alias; others used default embed rate. Explains partial invoice delta.
Edge note: console UI did not show pricing_tag since console reads enterprise_pricing_id only, not alias-inferred tags. This mismatch confused account team and customer.

Repro: replaying raw postbacks through reconciler in staging re-applied 'eco-v1' when enterprise_pricing_id absent. Removing 'eco-v1' alias from mapping yields expected enterprise rate in replayed runs.
Potential root cause: an alias rule was added to cover legacy free-tier mapping but the rule's scope included enterprise embed route due to a wildcard route match (embed-*).
resolution_summary: Provisional credit issued and alias mapping rolled back. Permanent fix is to scope alias rule to non-enterprise routes and to update reconciler to prefer explicit enterprise_pricing_id over aliases. Billing re-rated affected postbacks and submitted adjustment to accounting for $3,200 credit. Customer notified.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-11 12:25 - Action: Created provisional credit PC-8712 for $3,200 applied to ClearVoice AI account (pending final adjustment).
2026-03-11 17:40 - Action: Rolled back alias change from PR #2891 (reverted commit 7a1c4d) to remove eco-v1 from default alias set.
2026-03-12 02:15 - Action: Updated reconciler to prioritize enterprise_pricing_id when present; added unit tests around alias scoping for embed routes (PR #2910).

2026-03-12 07:50 - Action: Replayed affected postbacks in staging and in production re-rating job; confirmed adjusted invoice lines show negotiated embed rate. Final accounting adjustment scheduled for next billing cycle and customer invoice will be corrected with a credit memo.
next_steps: 1) Follow up with accounting to issue final credit memo and close provisional credit upon reconciliation (owner: Billing Team).
2) Coordinate a short postmortem doc in Confluence to capture the alias scoping regression and preventative tests (owner: SRE).
3) Add console visibility for inferred pricing_tag on postback detail page so customers and CS can see when alias inference occurs (owner: Console team).
4) Notify GTM & AM teams of rollback and credit details so customer-facing comms are consistent (owner: CS Manager).
